title: TIP RED 1193 red journey with the creation hold, d1 typed before the new view has the keyboard: the smoke gate's steps 1-18 (on debug.key), then debug.creation.hold of the first Cmd-D's creation, Cmd-D, d1 at once, Cmd-D, d2 at once, release, and step 23's checks: each line in its own new pane
why: TIP RED 1193 (STATUS 1202, 1226): the second Cmd-D's keys go to the FIRST new pane while creation 1 is still pending. The P0 owner's DEBUG hook debug.creation.hold {n: 1} keeps creation 1's daemon reply until release (cmux-ad 11:25Z), so the second Cmd-D and the d2 keys are typed while creation 1 is pending in EVERY round, with no hog and no product timing change. smoke_hold_path runs after step 23's checks (so a red is never hidden) and proves the hold path from the hook's release reply: creation 1 was still pending and creation 2 had started. Each key's path (handled_by, trace) is recorded as data. A build without the hook is not run. On #29301's red ref (base product code) step 23 must fail every round; on its head it must pass every round. After the first Cmd-D the journey waits (at most 5 s) until AppKit's first responder is the first new pane's terminal view (debug.focus), as the P0 owner asked (11:3xZ): then d1, the second Cmd-D and d2 go straight through while creation 1 is held, so creation 2 starts while creation 1 is pending (the race) in every round. The proof needs the hook's release reply to show resumed [1] (creation 1 really waited) and started >= 2. Variant 'early' (pa-d 11:4xZ): no wait after the first Cmd-D, so d1 is typed while the new pane's view does not have the keyboard yet, as in the failing smoke rounds of 5097a275a876 (STATUS 1226: d1's keys held). The 'wait' variant passed on the red ref 25b488f6607 (STATUS 1384).
